title: Balanced Brackets
description:
# Balanced Brackets

A string of brackets is **balanced** when every opening bracket has a matching closing bracket of the same type, and pairs are properly nested.

The bracket types are `()`, `[]`, and `{}`.

## Input

A single line containing only bracket characters (the line may be empty).

```
([{}])
```

## Output

Print `YES` if the brackets are balanced, otherwise `NO`.

```
YES
```

## Examples

| Input      | Output | Why |
|------------|--------|-----|
| `()[]{}`   | `YES`  | each pair closes immediately |
| `([{}])`   | `YES`  | properly nested |
| `(]`       | `NO`   | mismatched types |
| `([)]`     | `NO`   | wrong nesting order |
| `(((`      | `NO`   | never closed |

## Think about

- The last bracket you opened must be the first one you close. What data structure has that "last in, first out" behaviour?
starterCode:
s = input()

# TODO: print "YES" if the brackets in s are balanced, otherwise "NO"
hints: The last bracket you open must be the first one you close - that's a stack.
Push every opening bracket. For each closing bracket, the top of the stack must be its matching opener; pop it. At the end the stack must be empty. (Same stack idea as Evaluate Postfix.)

```
let stack be empty
for each character c in s
    if c is an opening bracket
        push c onto stack
    else
        if stack is empty or top of stack does not match c
            print "NO" and stop
        pop stack
if stack is empty then print "YES" else print "NO"
```
